name: bridge-pier
$comment: A two-span truss bridge on a centre pier with a lorry: the overloaded 40 t lorry buckles the slender diagonal 27 next to the pier, its X-partner takes the panel shear and the redundant truss carries on; with weaker members the chords and posts next to it fail, the pier column buckles and the bridge collapses.

parameters.name: strength
parameters.description: Strength factor of every member: scales the tensile strength fy and the buckling loads

parameters.name: slender
parameters.description: Buckling capacity of diagonal 27 (next to the pier) as a fraction of its design section (I = slender x 1.5e-05 m^4)

parameters.name: m_truck
parameters.description: Lorry mass (both trusses; each carries half)

parameters.name: k_tyre
parameters.description: Tyre stiffness per axle and truss

parameters.name: x_start
parameters.description: Start position of the lorry's centre of mass

parameters.name: y_start
parameters.description: Centre-of-mass height over the unloaded tyres at the start

options.text:
A lorry crosses a 2 x 24 m truss bridge on a steel column in the river. The truss is continuous over the pier and the two panels next to it are X-braced, so it is **redundant**: one failed member need not bring it down. Diagonal 27, next to the pier, is **too slender**: it holds a 20 t lorry, but the overloaded 40 t lorry buckles it, and its X-partner (bar 26) takes over the panel shear.

Lower the **strength** of all members and the redistributed load is too much: the post and the bottom chord next to the buckled diagonal fail, then the pier column buckles, and the bridge collapses. Every change runs the model again.

cards.title: Deflection: left span, pier, right span
